lines: At 9:14 p.m., according to every clock in the shop, Matthias Brandt was winding the grandfather clock in the window.
At 9:14 p.m., according to the coroner, the landlord was dying in the room above.
The two facts sat together like an unlit match and a barrel of oil.
Inspector Reyes had been in the shop for an hour.
The clocks, forty of them, ticked at slightly different speeds, so that the room seemed to be whispering.
"You were here all evening," she said.
"Every clock will tell you something," said Brandt, with a clockmaker's gentle melancholy.
She stopped in front of the grandfather clock.
It was the only one in the room running perfectly on time, which is what bothered her.
A man who loves clocks does not keep one honest and let thirty-nine drift.
"The clock says you were here," she said.
"But it's the only one that's right.
You corrected it tonight, Mr. Brandt, and a man doesn't correct a clock for himself.
He corrects it for a witness."
